itinerary: Row colours follow the category (col J):  🚃 yellow = transport · 🍜 peach = food · 🏛 lilac = culture · 🛍 pink = shopping · 🌿 green = nature · 🟣 purple = Day 10 'choose one'  ·  RM auto-converts from the rate on the Overview tab
Immigration + baggage claim. Exchange some yen at airport (ok rate). Better: use 7-Eleven ATM in city. Get ICOCA card at station.

Nankai Rapi:t from KIX → Namba (38 min, ~¥1,490/person incl. reserved seat — luggage space, comfy). Budget option: Nankai Airport Express (¥970, ~45 min, no reservation, IC card OK). ⚠️ The JR Haruka does NOT go to Namba.

🏨 Sample Hotel Osaka — Osaka Metro Sennichimae Line from Namba → Nagata Station (~8 min). Hotel is 250m from Nagata Station. Check-in is usually 15:00 — leave bags at front desk, freshen up. Lawson konbini is walking distance to the right of hotel.

🍲 Chitose 千とせ — Osaka's famous 'nikusui' (meat udon soup without the noodles), friend's rec! Main shop (Namba Sennichimae) closes ~14:30 & shuts Tue; if queue is long, Chitose Bekkan inside Namba Grand Kagetsu is open 11:00–20:00. 🛍 Then 3COINS (¥300 lifestyle shop) — branches in Namba CITY / Namba Parks, right by the station. First shopping stop as soon as we land!
Glico Running Man sign • Takoyaki at Kukuru (¥700) — crispy outside, molten inside • Ebisu Bridge photos • Channel-side walk.

Japan's longest covered arcade (~600 m). 💊 Drugstore run: Matsumoto Kiyoshi, Daikoku Drug, Sundrug etc. line the arcade — supplements, meds, sunscreen (Biore UV, Anessa, Skin Aqua) & skincare. Tax-free over ¥5,000 per store with passport — compare prices between shops. 🥛 Look out for Japanese yoghurt in a bag (friend's rec) here & in supermarkets/konbini.

Ancient stone lane with moss-covered Fudo Myo-o statue, lantern-lit at night. Dinner: Kushikatsu at Daruma or okonomiyaki at Mizuno. Or back near hotel: 🍗 宮崎地鶏料理専門店 (izakaya till 11pm) • 🥟 Gyoza no Ohsho Nagata (till 11pm).
Konbini breakfast: onigiri, egg sandwich, canned coffee. Surprisingly great!
Late October = stunning autumn foliage around the moat. Castle museum covers samurai history & Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Lift to top for panoramic city views.
🍛 Friend's rec! Tiny counter shop near Namba — curry rice & curry ramen, crispy katsu, cheese & spicy sausage toppings. Order at ticket machine (bring cash).
Kitchen of Osaka' — fresh tuna sashimi on a stick, wagyu skewers, tamagoyaki, giant scallops. Sample as you walk. Hei Yin
Anime figures, retro Famicom games, gunpla model kits. Very affordable versus Tokyo.
Retro 1950s neighbourhood. Tower: 103 m, 360° views, Billiken lucky statue. Try fugu (blowfish) here if feeling adventurous!
Osaka's iconic savory pancake. Must-eat. Try Mizuno or Kiji — Osaka originals. Bonito flakes 'dance' on top from the heat.
Osaka Metro from Nagata → Namba (Sennichimae Line, ~8 min), transfer walk to Nankai Namba Station (~5-7 min), then Nankai Main Line → Sumiyoshi Taisha Station (~9-10 min). IC card accepted.

One of Japan's oldest shrines (founded 211 AD), unique Sumiyoshi-zukuri architecture predating Buddhist influence. Iconic arched Taiko-bashi (Drum Bridge) over the pond — striking photo spot. Four main shrine halls are National Treasures. Peaceful grounds, far fewer crowds than Fushimi Inari.
Local udon or teishoku set near the shrine approach.

Head to Umeda. LUCUA, Grand Front Osaka & Loft for skincare, sunscreen & cosmetics; big drugstores around Umeda/Osaka Stn for supplements & meds (top up anything missed on Day 1). Grand Front food hall for a snack break.
Floating Garden Observatory' — 40th floor glass tunnel escalator between two towers. 360° views, spectacular at sunset (~17:30 in October).
Giant red Ferris wheel ON TOP of the mall. HEP Five for fashion, Grand Front Osaka for upscale goods and food hall.

ORITAYA Lucua Ire (LUCUA 1100) branch in Osaka
10F Lucua Dining, 3-1-3 Umeda, Kita Ward, Osaka, Osaka Prefecture 530-0001
From Nagata: Chuo Line → Hommachi, change to Midosuji Line → Umeda (~25 min). Walk to JR Osaka → JR Special Rapid (shinkaisoku) to Kyoto (~29 min, ¥580/person, no reservation).

🏨 Sample Hotel Kyoto (Kameoka) is 25 min from Kyoto by JR (check-in tonight). Store bags at Kyoto Station coin lockers (¥400–¥700/bag, B1 near Karasuma exit). Tip: lockers fill up by late morning in autumn — the luggage counter is backup.
Kyoto's Kitchen' — 390 m covered arcade. Tsukemono pickles, grilled mochi, tamagoyaki, soy milk donuts, fresh tofu, sake samples. Go at lunchtime — many stalls close ~17:00.

⭐ UNMISSABLE — 10,000 vermillion torii gates! Go at least to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (~45 min up) for city views; gates thinner & less crowded the higher you go. Look for fox (kitsune) statues everywhere.

⭐ Kiyomizu-dera (closes ~18:00, ¥500/person) — wooden stage over autumn maples, sunset views over Kyoto. Then walk down Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka (Higashiyama old streets) → Yasaka Shrine → Gion Hanamikoji at dusk — best chance to spot maiko/geisha until ~19:00. Don't block paths for photos!
Atmospheric narrow alley along Kamogawa River. Try obanzai (Kyoto small-dish cuisine, like Japanese tapas). Many restaurants have outdoor river terraces.
JR San'in Line to Kameoka, 25 min

Collect bags from Kyoto Station coin locker → JR San'in Line (Sagano Line) from Kyoto → Kameoka Station (25 min, ¥400/person). Sample Hotel Kyoto is 2 min walk from Kameoka Station exit. ⭐ TOMORROW: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is only 15–20 min away from here by JR — perfect for the early morning visit!
Quick konbini breakfast or hotel breakfast if available early. ⭐ Early start today — Arashiyama at dawn is the goal.

⭐ BONUS from Kameoka: Arashiyama is only 3 stops away on JR San'in/Sagano Line (15–20 min, ¥240/person) — much closer than from central Kyoto! Walk 10 min from Saga-Arashiyama Station to bamboo grove entrance.
⭐ Arrive at opening — ethereal before crowds hit. The wind through bamboo sounds incredible. Look for the natural frames and long corridor shots. Walk toward Okochi Sanso Villa gate.
UNESCO Heritage site. Sogenchi garden designed 700 years ago — autumn maples reflected in the pond are spectacular.
Hidden gem — steep hillside temple with pagoda views over Arashiyama. Less visited, arguably the best autumn foliage spot in the area.
🍵 Friend's rec! Tea house near Togetsukyo Bridge — matcha sweets, parfaits & Kyoto-style lunch sets. Popular — expect a queue at peak lunch. Backup: yudofu or kiri mochi along the main street.
Top two floors covered in real gold leaf. Reflection in Kyokochi Pond = the iconic shot. Go afternoon when morning rush fades.
World's most famous zen garden — 15 stones on white gravel, one always hidden from view. Quiet and meditative. Closes 17:00.
Bus to JR Hanazono, JR to Kameoka ~35 min
Short break at the hotel after an early start. Kameoka is quiet — a nice change from central Kyoto crowds.

Friend's rec! Kameoka's hot-spring area is ~10 min from Kameoka Stn. Several ryokan offer day-use baths (higaeri onsen) — check hours & book ahead, many stop day-use by ~19:00–20:00. Some have private family baths (kashikiri) for couples. Tattoos may not be allowed.
Local izakaya or ramen near Kameoka Station, or a kaiseki dinner at the onsen ryokan if booking a day-use + meal plan.
DAY 6  ·  Thu 29 Oct  ·  NARA DAY TRIP
JR San'in/Sagano Line: Kameoka → Kyoto Station (25 min, ¥400/person).
Kintetsu Limited Express from Kyoto → Kintetsu Nara (¥1,170/person, 35 min) — faster and drops nearer the park. Or JR Nara Line (¥720, 45 min).
⭐ 1,200 semi-wild deer roam free! Buy shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200/pack) — the deer have learned to bow for food. Extremely photogenic. Guard your snacks in your bag!
Japan's largest bronze Buddha (15 m). The wooden hall is the world's largest wooden building. Find the 'Buddha's Nostril' pillar — if you fit through the hole, you get enlightenment!
Try kakinoha-zushi (sushi in persimmon leaf — Nara's unique speciality). Warabi mochi for dessert.
3,000 bronze and stone lanterns lining the approach. UNESCO listed. Beautiful autumn maple corridor.
Traditional garden using 'borrowed scenery' (shakkei) with Mt. Wakakusa as backdrop. Peaceful and less touristy. Last entry ~16:00.
Kintetsu Nara → Kyoto Station (~35–45 min), then bus 5/17 or subway to the Ginkaku-ji end of the path (~30 min). Arrive around sunset (~17:10).
2 km canal-side walk lined with maple trees, from Ginkaku-ji south towards Nanzen-ji. Named after philosopher Nishida Kitaro. Romantic at dusk.
Last night in Kyoto — treat yourselves! Kaiseki set dinner or quality sushi omakase (book ahead). Afterwards: JR San'in Line from Kyoto → Kameoka (25 min).
Last morning at Sample Hotel Kyoto (Kameoka). Quick breakfast, checkout.
JR San'in Line: Kameoka → Kyoto Station (25 min, ¥400/person).
Nozomi is fastest (2h 15 min). Reserve seats! Sit D/E side (right facing Tokyo) for Mt. Fuji views around Shin-Fuji Station.
Store luggage if room not ready. Try Tokyo Station's underground Ramen Street — B1 level. 8 famous ramen shops in one corridor.
Tokyo's oldest temple (628 AD). Kaminarimon Thunder Gate red lantern = most photographed spot in Tokyo. Nakamise Shopping St for ningyo-yaki, fans, kimonos.

Golden Gai — 6 narrow alleyways packed with ~200 tiny atmospheric bars, each fitting 5–8 people. Incredible for bar-hopping. • Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — smoky yakitori stalls crammed under the train tracks, super nostalgic • Kabukicho neon district — Tokyo's most over-the-top entertainment area, great for photos • East Shinjuku side streets for just wandering.

⭐ Eat right on Memory Lane — tiny stalls serving yakitori, offal skewers, beer under a haze of charcoal smoke. Super atmospheric, very affordable, quintessential Tokyo. Arrive early as stalls fill fast by 20:00.
Vast forested sanctuary amid the Tokyo metropolis. 700 m tree-lined path to the shrine. Serene morning walk before a busy day.

Wild Tokyo street fashion, crepe shops, rainbow cotton candy, mochi donuts. 💄 @cosme TOKYO (right by Harajuku Stn) — 3 floors of Japanese skincare, sunscreen & makeup with rankings of best-sellers. Tax-free with passport.
Upscale boulevard with good cafes. Try any international or Japanese restaurants here.
World's busiest pedestrian crossing — up to 3,000 people at once. Best viewed from 2F Starbucks (queue for window seat!) or Scramble Square rooftop deck.

⭐ YODOBASHI-AKIBA (9 floors — cameras, drones, audio, laptops, gaming, appliances, all tax-free with passport) • BIC CAMERA Akihabara (separate building, great for phones & accessories) • SOFMAP (multiple stores — used electronics, retro consoles, trade-ins) • LAOX (electronics + duty-free for tourists) • YAMADA DENKI Akihabara for price comparison. Anime & figure shops scattered throughout — easy to pop in between stores. Tax-free on purchases over ¥5,000 with passport. Tip: check kakaku.com beforehand and screenshot prices to use as leverage.

Even without costumes, an incredible spectacle — thousands of wildly dressed people flood Center-gai and Dogenzaka. Great for crowd-watching and photos. Note: open-container alcohol banned since 2023, but bars inside are all open. Peak craziness hits around 21:00–23:00.
DAY 9  ·  Sun 1 Nov  ·  KAMAKURA DAY TRIP
Go a bit earlier — Kamakura is popular on weekends.
JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station (1 stop from Kanda) → Kamakura, direct, ~1 hr, ~¥950/person. IC card accepted. Weekend — leave early to beat day-trip crowds.
Iconic outdoor bronze Great Buddha — 13.35 m, cast 1252 AD. You can go INSIDE the hollow statue (¥50/person extra). Peaceful mountain backdrop.
⭐ Stunning hillside temple with panoramic ocean & city views. Huge golden Kannon statue (9.18 m). Cave with 1,000 small Kannon figures. Beautiful autumn foliage.
⭐ Kamakura's signature dish — shirasu (baby whitebait) on rice, raw or cooked. Fresh from Sagami Bay. Try Maruichi Shokudo or restaurants on Komachi-dori Street.
Kamakura's most important shrine, at head of long approach avenue lined with cherry (now maple) trees. Great views back down to the sea.
Small, peaceful bamboo grove — unlike Arashiyama, you can have matcha tea inside the grove itself! ¥300 entry + ¥600 matcha in the garden. Totally worth it.
Try Japanese-style yakiniku — grill your own wagyu at the table. Great way to celebrate the trip.
⭐ Best breakfast in Tokyo! Fresh sushi/sashimi, tamagoyaki, oysters, tuna rice bowls. Before leaving: check out of the hotel (~11:00 limit) and leave bags at front desk — or check out now if easier.
🟣  CHOOSE ONE MORNING ACTIVITY  —  Pick whichever appeals to you!
Futuristic waterfront: life-size Gundam RX-78 statue (FREE), DiverCity mall, teamLab Museum (skip — done before), Tokyo Big Sight, Palette Town. Yurikamome monorail is scenic.
Nostalgic pre-war Tokyo neighbourhood that survived WWII bombings. Old temples, cat statues everywhere, artisan craft shops, quiet alleyways. Feels like a different era. FREE to wander.
Traditional Edo-period garden right on Tokyo Bay with autumn foliage. Matcha teahouse inside (¥500 entry + ¥700 matcha). Peaceful contrast to busy Tokyo.
Final souvenir run: Don Quijote (Donki, open 24 hrs), Shinjuku, or Akihabara. Best for last-minute omiyage (Japanese snacks, cosmetics, Kit Kat varieties, stationery).
Hotel checkout is ~11:00 — bags should already be with the front desk.
Don Quijote for final omiyage haul — snacks, cosmetics, quirky gifts. Last chance for drugstore/skincare top-ups. Collect bags from hotel ~16:30.
Last proper Japanese meal — make it count!
Tokyo Monorail from Hamamatsucho → Haneda T3 International (20 min). Or Keikyu from Shinagawa.
Air Asia X check-in opens ~3 hrs before. Haneda T3 has excellent duty free: Japanese whisky, Kit Kats, cosmetics. At gate by 22:30.
Air Asia X → KLIA. Arrive KL 06:50 (+1 day). Safe travels! 🎌
